rules.title: HTML injected into the DOM without sanitization
rules.why: These sinks bypass the framework's automatic escaping; untrusted content reaching them executes as script.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Closed when the value passes through DOMPurify or an equivalent sanitizer immediately before the sink, or is a compile-time literal. Trace the value.

rules.title: Dynamic code evaluation
rules.why: Evaluating request-influenced strings is remote code execution on the server or in the victim's browser.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Ignore RegExp.prototype.exec (a regex match, not evaluation) and eval over hard-coded literals.

rules.title: Shell command executed from Node
rules.why: exec() runs through a shell; any interpolated request value becomes a command.
rules.falsePositiveHints: execFile/spawn with an argument ARRAY and shell:false is the safe form and not a finding. exec() with a template literal is.

rules.title: NoSQL query built from a raw request object
rules.why: Passing a request object straight into a query lets a caller submit operators such as {"$ne": null} or {"$gt": ""} to bypass filters, including authentication.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Closed when fields are explicitly picked and cast, or a schema validator (Joi/Zod/express-validator) runs first.

rules.title: No authentication or authorization middleware detected
rules.why: An HTTP API with no authentication layer is fully anonymous.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Auth may be handled by an API gateway or reverse proxy. Verify rather than assume; state the assumption if unverifiable.

rules.title: Permissive CORS configuration
rules.why: cors() with no options allows every origin. Combined with credentials it exposes authenticated responses to any site.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Severity rises to High when credentials:true is also present, and falls to Low for a genuinely public read-only API.

rules.title: Security headers middleware absent
rules.why: Without CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors and HSTS the browser applies no defense-in-depth for the app.
rules.falsePositiveHints: May be set at the CDN or proxy. Verify.

rules.title: JWT verification weakened or absent
rules.why: jwt.decode does not verify the signature - a forged token is accepted. 'none' algorithm and ignored expiry are equally fatal.
rules.falsePositiveHints: jwt.decode is acceptable for reading a token the app already verified in the same request. Confirm a verify() precedes it.

rules.title: Session or cookie flags weakened
rules.why: A session cookie without httpOnly is readable by injected script; without secure it travels in cleartext.
rules.falsePositiveHints: secure:false is expected in a local-development branch - confirm it is environment-gated.

rules.title: Recursive merge or dynamic property assignment (prototype pollution)
rules.why: Merging attacker-controlled keys can set __proto__ and change behavior application-wide, sometimes reaching RCE.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Closed when __proto__/constructor/prototype keys are rejected, Object.create(null) is used, or the source is trusted.

rules.title: Outbound request built from request data
rules.why: SSRF reaches internal services and the cloud metadata endpoint from inside the perimeter.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Closed if the host is fixed and only the path varies, or the URL is checked against a host allow-list.

rules.title: Declared dependencies to inventory for advisory checking
rules.why: Collects the dependency inventory for the Step 4 advisory check.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Not a finding on its own. Note whether a lockfile is committed - its absence is itself a supply-chain weakness (A08).
